record.bible_text: <FO><FO>To the chief Musician<WH05329><WTH8764> upon Gittith<WH01665>, <FI>A Psalm<Fi> of Asaph<WH0623>.<Fo><Fo> Sing aloud<WH07442><WTH8685> unto God<WH0430> our strength<WH05797>: make a joyful noise<WH07321><WTH8685> unto the God<WH0430> of Jacob<WH03290>. <RF>of Asaph: or, for Asaph<Rf>
Take<WH05375><WTH8798> a psalm<WH02172>, and bring<WH05414><WTH8798> hither the timbrel<WH08596>, the pleasant<WH05273> harp<WH03658> with the psaltery<WH05035>.
Blow up<WH08628><WTH8798> the trumpet<WH07782> in the new moon<WH02320>, in the time appointed<WH03677>, on our solemn feast<WH02282> day<WH03117>.
For this <FI>was<Fi> a statute<WH02706> for Israel<WH03478>, <FI>and<Fi> a law<WH04941> of the God<WH0430> of Jacob<WH03290>.

This he ordained<WH07760><WTH8804> in Joseph<WH03084> <FI>for<Fi> a testimony<WH05715>, when he went out<WH03318><WTH8800> through the land<WH0776> of Egypt<WH04714>: <FI>where<Fi> I heard<WH08085><WTH8799> a language<WH08193> <FI>that<Fi> I understood<WH03045><WTH8804> not. <RF>through: or, against<Rf>
I removed<WH05493><WTH8689> his shoulder<WH07926> from the burden<WH05447>: his hands<WH03709> were delivered<WH05674><WTH8799> from the pots<WH01731>. <RF>were...: Heb. passed away<Rf>

Thou calledst<WH07121><WTH8804> in trouble<WH06869>, and I delivered<WH02502><WTH8762> thee; I answered<WH06030><WTH8799> thee in the secret place<WH05643> of thunder<WH07482>: I proved<WH0974><WTH8799> thee at the waters<WH04325> of Meribah<WH04809>. Selah<WH05542>. <RF>Meribah: or, Strife<Rf><CM>
Hear<WH08085><WTH8798>, O my people<WH05971>, and I will testify<WH05749><WTH8686> unto thee: O Israel<WH03478>, if thou wilt hearken<WH08085><WTH8799> unto me;
There shall no strange<WH02114><WTH8801> god<WH0410> be in thee; neither shalt thou worship<WH07812><WTH8691> any strange<WH05236> god<WH0410>.

I <FI>am<Fi> the LORD<WH03068> thy God<WH0430>, which brought<WH05927><WTH8688> thee out of the land<WH0776> of Egypt<WH04714>: open thy mouth<WH06310> wide<WH07337><WTH8685>, and I will fill<WH04390><WTH8762> it.
But my people<WH05971> would not hearken<WH08085><WTH8804> to my voice<WH06963>; and Israel<WH03478> would<WH014><WTH8804> none of me.

So I gave them up<WH07971><WTH8762> unto their own hearts<WH03820>' lust<WH08307>: <FI>and<Fi> they walked<WH03212><WTH8799> in their own counsels<WH04156>. <RF>unto...: or, to the hardness of their hearts, or, imagination<Rf>
Oh<WH03863> that my people<WH05971> had hearkened<WH08085><WTH8802> unto me, <FI>and<Fi> Israel<WH03478> had walked<WH01980><WTH8762> in my ways<WH01870>!
I should soon<WH04592> have subdued<WH03665><WTH8686> their enemies<WH0341><WTH8802>, and turned<WH07725><WTH8686> my hand<WH03027> against their adversaries<WH06862>.

The haters<WH08130><WTH8764> of the LORD<WH03068> should have submitted<WH03584><WTH8762> themselves unto him: but their time<WH06256> should have endured for ever<WH05769>. <RF>submitted...: or, yielded feigned obedience: Heb. lied<Rf>

He should have fed<WH0398><WTH8686> them also with the finest<WH02459> of the wheat<WH02406>: and with honey<WH01706> out of the rock<WH06697> should I have satisfied<WH07646><WTH8686> thee. <RF>finest...: Heb. fat of wheat<Rf><CM>
